lines.trans: I came to pick up my belongings.
Are you holding up okay?
To be honest, I was disappointed.
All my plans were thrown off track—it's the worst.
My life is completely ruined, to the point where it's not even funny.
Still, I don't regret coming here.
Because even though it was only for a short while, it was so much fun.

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Godan verb; コミュニケーションを取る means 'to communicate'.

examples.text: よく連絡を取っています。
メモを取ってもいいですか。

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Irregular verb: くる -> きます -> きました.
Core everyday reassurance or check covering safety, health, and reliability.

examples.text: 心配しないで、大丈夫だよ。
examples.trans: Do not worry, it is fine.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

examples.text: がっかりさせないでよって。
examples.trans: And she says don't disappoint her.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: With で (全部で), means 'in total' or 'altogether'.

examples.text: 最悪の事態だ。もうどうなっても知りませんよ。
examples.trans: This is the worst possible outcome. Don't blame me for whatever happens now.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Refers to a person's life, career, and experiences.

examples.text: 人生を諦めないでください。
examples.trans: Please don't give up on life.

examples.text: 人生パーですよ、笑えないくらい。
examples.trans: My life is completely ruined, to the point where it's not even funny.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?
You are going to regret this.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Points to the place where the speaker currently stands.

examples.text: ここに座ってください。

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Calls someone's attention ('look here!') or asks for a brief pause (ちょっと待って).

examples.text: ちょっと待ってください。
ちょっと見てください。

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Connects a contrasting fact or trails off at the end of a sentence to voice a polite objection.

examples.text: お風呂に入りましたけど。
examples.trans: I already took a bath, though.

examples.text: 高いけど、おいしいです。

meanings.note: Plain い-adjective.

examples.text: 彼の英語は本当にすごい。

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Attaches to pronouns or people nouns (僕ら, 彼ら).
Used with が before it (ストーリーが必要だ 'a story is needed') or な before a noun.
Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

examples.text: 黒木さん、私のことも最初から全部見透かしてて。
examples.trans: Ms. Kuroki saw right through me from the very beginning.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Colloquial particle adding emphasis, similar to でも or も.

examples.text: 俺だって言いたいことがある。
examples.trans: I have something I want to say too.

examples.text: 誰だって間違いはある。

meanings.note: 分かってる asks or states ongoing understanding; plain past 分かった means 'got it! / I understand'.

examples.text: 日本語が少し分かります。

examples.trans: Got it, I will come right away.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.en: to think; to feel; to believe
meanings.note: Often follows quotative と to express an opinion or belief.

examples.text: それはいいと思います。
あの作品を超えるのはそう簡単じゃありません。
examples.trans: Surpassing that debut film of ours won't be easy.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.
Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun for place.
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
